subject: Emotions
title: Courage Under Fire
description: A quick, practical guide to Courage Under Fire.

hook.text: Firefighters feel fear every time they enter a burning building. They act anyway. That's not fearlessness.

buildup.text: Neuroscience shows courageous people feel the same fear as everyone else. Their brains just regulate it better.

discovery.text: The subgenual anterior cingulate cortex overrides the amygdala during brave acts. Courage has a brain address.

twist.text: Studies of Medal of Honor recipients show most don't recall deciding to be brave. They describe acting automatically.

climax.text: Courage is trainable. Repeated practice in stressful conditions builds the neural pathways that override fear.

punchline.text: Bravery isn't feeling no fear. It's acting before fear decides.

quiz.question: What do brain scans of courageous people show?
